speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; can you describe exactly how your balance and coordination are affected when you walk?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That describes a classic "drunken gait." You mentioned the symptoms are worse on the right side; does the clumsiness in your arms and legs also affect your fine motor skills, like buttoning a shirt or writing? Additionally, have you noticed any issues with your speech or difficulty swallowing recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

The combination of new-onset ataxia, worsening on the right side, and your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly suspicious for PML. I need to confirm the extent of white matter involvement immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_with_contrast. REQUEST TEST: JC_virus_antibody_in_serum.
